source_name: NBS – Zoznam dohliadaných subjektov (subjekty.nbs.sk)
why_relevant: Central NBS database of all supervised entities across sectors incl. banking, payment services and e-money. Enumerates every licensed bank, foreign-bank branch, payment institution, e-money institution and agent in SK, which is the actor list every A5 (jobs/leadership) collection cell needs. Site advertises a downloadable database ('Databáza na stiahnutie'), and search results referenced an API endpoint pattern under subjekty.nbs.sk/api/.

source_name: NBS – Registre (hub of all NBS supervisory registers)
why_relevant: Top-level index of every register NBS maintains; the cheapest way to snowball into new register endpoints (PSD2, RBUZ, register informácií/DORA, financial intermediaries) rather than guessing URLs.

source_name: NBS – Register podľa PSD2 (payment institutions, e-money institutions, agents)
why_relevant: Statutory PSD2 register: the legally mandated national list of payment institutions, limited-scope providers, e-money institutions, AISPs and their agents. Underpins the payments half of the sector scope and feeds the EBA central register.

source_name: NBS – Výroky právoplatných rozhodnutí (final enforceable supervisory decisions)
why_relevant: The single highest-value A5 source in this cell: a filterable table of NBS decisions with issue date, entity, decision number and date of legal force, filterable by IČO, year/month, decision area and decision type. Historically these decision texts name individuals granted prior consent (predchádzajúci súhlas) to be elected to a bank's board or appointed as a senior employee reporting to the statutory body — i.e. named appointments, dated, often ahead of the bank's own press release. Also carries sanction decisions naming officers.

source_name: NBS – Archív rozhodnutí (decision archive)
why_relevant: Historical backfill for the decision register — needed to build a multi-year time series of who was approved into which seat and when, and to establish tenure baselines.

source_name: NBS – Výroky neprávoplatných vykonateľných rozhodnutí
why_relevant: Decisions that are enforceable but not yet final — an EARLIER signal than the final-decisions register. Useful as a leading indicator of enforcement naming officers and of pending governance changes.

source_name: NBS – historical PDF compendia of decision operative parts (útvar dohľadu nad finančným trhom)
why_relevant: Pre-portal era PDFs collecting the operative parts of NBS decisions by year. Search snippets showed these explicitly contain prior-consent decisions naming individuals elected as board members / appointed as senior employees at named Slovak banks — a proven template for what the modern register contains and a source of long-run history.

source_name: NBS – individual sanction decision PDFs (ofsrozhodnutia)
why_relevant: Full-text sanction decisions published as PDFs under a predictable path. Full texts, unlike the summary table, can name responsible officers and describe governance failures.

source_name: Vestník NBS (NBS official bulletin, annual volumes)
why_relevant: Official bulletin carrying NBS opatrenia and notices, including the measures that define what a prior-consent application under §28 of the Banking Act must contain. Sets the legal frame that makes the fit-and-proper record exist, and is where procedural changes (e.g. Opatrenie 1/2025) that alter the data trail are announced.

source_name: NBS – legislation detail: Opatrenie 1/2025 amending Opatrenie 6/2010 on §28 prior-consent applications
why_relevant: Documents exactly which fit-and-proper facts a bank must file with NBS when appointing board members and key function holders — i.e. defines the structure and richness of the underlying record set the A5 workstream mines.

source_name: NBS – Upozornenie: predchádzajúci súhlas na kvalifikovanú účasť
why_relevant: Notices/instructions section of NBS. Qualifying-holding consents precede ownership changes, which are the most reliable leading indicator of subsequent board turnover at Slovak banks and payment institutions.

source_name: NBS – Banking supervision section (EN mirror)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of the banking supervision area; useful for entity-name normalisation and for confirming SSM/NBS division of labour (which SK banks are ECB-significant vs NBS-supervised LSIs), which determines whether an appointment approval will surface at NBS or ECB.

source_name: NBS – Banková rada / Bank Board pages (incl. former members)
why_relevant: The regulator's own leadership. Governor and vice-governors are appointed by the President on a government proposal approved by parliament; other members by the government on the governor's proposal. Vacancies on the Bank Board (search indicated an under-strength board) directly affect the pace of fit-and-proper decisions and are themselves A5 leadership-move events. A 'former members' page gives clean historical tenure data.

source_name: NBS – Aktuality (press releases / news)
why_relevant: NBS narrative channel; announces market-structure moves such as opening payment systems to non-bank PSPs, which drives new entrants, new licences and consequent hiring. Provides dated context around register changes.

source_name: NBS – Register informácií (DORA ICT third-party register)
why_relevant: DORA register of information on ICT third-party arrangements. Indirect A5 relevance: reveals which vendors serve which Slovak financial entities and which functions are outsourced — a strong proxy for where internal teams are being built vs outsourced, and a named-contact/function-owner surface.

source_name: NBS – Informácie dohliadaných subjektov o rokovaniach valného zhromaždenia, dozornej rady, štatutárneho orgánu
why_relevant: Supervised entities must notify NBS about general meetings and sessions of the supervisory board and statutory body. This is precisely the governance-event stream behind board changes. Found in the insurance section — needs checking whether an equivalent exists for banking/payments, but the mechanism is directly on-topic.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision – List of supervised entities (SSM), incl. Slovak SIs/LSIs
why_relevant: Authoritative, periodically republished list separating significant institutions (ECB-supervised, so fit-and-proper decided by ECB) from less significant institutions (NBS-decided). Determines which regulator's record to watch for a given Slovak bank's board appointment. Published in versioned PDFs and also as a landing page.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision – Supervisory sanctions / published sanctions and statistics
why_relevant: ECB and NCAs are legally required to publish supervisory sanctions. Covers sanctions imposed on Slovak significant institutions and those imposed by NBS at the ECB's request. Sanction texts and the accompanying annual sanctioning reports describe governance and management-body failings, sometimes naming roles.

source_name: ECB SSM Supervisory Manual (fit-and-proper / common procedures)
why_relevant: Explains how SSM fit-and-proper assessments are initiated by the NCA (NBS) and decided by the ECB, including timelines. Essential for interpreting the lag between an NBS filing and a public appointment, and for knowing which artefacts are ever public.

source_name: ECB – Decisions taken by the Governing Council (other decisions), multilingual incl. SK/CS
why_relevant: Regular ECB publication of non-monetary-policy decisions, which includes supervisory decisions and appointments/nominations relevant to national central banks and SSM bodies. Published in national languages including Slovak, giving bilingual name variants.

source_name: EBA – Register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2 (central register)
why_relevant: Aggregates the national PSD2 registers, updated at least daily by NCAs, fully downloadable in machine-readable format. Gives a normalised, diff-friendly SK payment/e-money actor list without scraping NBS HTML, and is the fallback if the NBS register is hard to parse.

source_name: EBA – Credit institutions register
why_relevant: EU/EEA-wide authorised credit institutions list including Slovak banks and branches; provides identifiers (LEI/authorisation numbers) for entity resolution across NBS, ECB and commercial-register sources.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (ORSR) – company extracts naming štatutárny orgán
why_relevant: The legally authoritative record of who sits on a Slovak bank's or payment institution's predstavenstvo and dozorná rada, with entry/exit dates. It is the confirmation leg after an NBS prior consent: consent first, then ORSR registration, then usually the press release. Free informative extracts per entity.

source_name: Obchodný vestník SR (Ministry of Justice commercial journal)
why_relevant: Official state publication organ where registrations of new and changed registered data are published without undue delay — explicitly including changes in the person of the statutory or supervisory body. Gives a dated, searchable EVENT stream rather than ORSR's current-state snapshot, so it is the better change-detection primitive.

source_name: registre.nbs.sk (NBS registry portal front door)
why_relevant: Separate NBS registry host alongside subjekty.nbs.sk; likely the entry point for register applications and possibly for machine-readable exports. Worth probing for stable endpoints before committing to HTML scraping.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (ORSR) — vyhľadávanie podľa obchodného mena
why_relevant: Legacy but still-primary public interface to the Slovak commercial register. Entity detail pages ('výpis') list štatutárny orgán (predstavenstvo / konateľ), prokúra, dozorná rada, organizačné zložky and share capital, each with a legal effective date (dátum vzniku/zániku funkcie). For banks, payment institutions and their SK subsidiaries this is the ground-truth record of every leadership and organisational change, usually available before or without any press release. Also exposes historical entries via 'úplný výpis'.

source_name: ORSR — vyhľadávanie podľa priezviska a mena osoby (person search)
why_relevant: Person-centric index over the commercial register: given a named executive, returns every SK entity where they are or were a registered officer. This is the single highest-value tool for tracking an individual banker's or payments executive's moves across entities, and for detecting new appointments by watching known-person profiles. Inverse of the entity-first view.

source_name: Elektronické služby Obchodného registra (sluzby.orsr.sk) — nový portál MS SR
why_relevant: The modernised Ministry of Justice ORSR portal (search + electronic filing services). Expected to be the long-term successor to orsr.sk and likely to expose cleaner, more structured entity views and document access; worth tracking in parallel so collection does not break when the legacy portal is retired.
